root_cause.instrumentation: Temporary [DEBUG-QUEUE] prints on the three rejection sites, reverted before the commit. Only the collector CHUNK branch fired: `collector CHUNK overflow request=2 depth=64 max=64`, with the mailbox growing 29 -> 62 -> 64 while the consumer drained one entry per drain(max_chunks=1) call.
root_cause.policy: Both engine-to-consumer queues were fixed at 64 entries and treated 'full' as 'cancel this child', so a consumer slower than the producer lost the request instead of slowing it down. Per-chunk telemetry roughly doubles the consumer's per-chunk cost, which is what put the consumer below the producer's rate.

after.change: The mailbox bound is the child's own output budget (floor = configured bound, hard cap 4096 entries), and a cancelled stream reports the usage it delivered.

follow_up: The consumer still pays one threadpool round trip per chunk (run_in_threadpool(_next_stream_item, iterator) in hipengine/server/api.py), so a slow client now buffers instead of dying. Batched draining is the throughput fix and is recorded in docs/REFACTOR.md.
